arxiv-2106-05182.creator: Manjari Dutta, Shreemoyee Ganguly, Sunandan Gangopadhyay
arxiv-2106-05182.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Manjari Dutta, Shreemoyee Ganguly, Sunandan Gangopadhyay. In this paper we have obtained the exact eigenstates of a two dimensional damped harmonic oscillator in the presence of an external magnetic field varying with respect to time in time dependent noncommutative space.

arxiv-2203-11336.creator: Jiahan Wang 1, Jörn Sesterhenn 2, Wolf-Christian Müller 1
arxiv-2203-11336.description: Abstract Coherent structures in two-dimensional Navier-Stokes turbulence are ubiquitously observed in nature, experiments and numerical simulations. The present study conducts a comparison between several structure detection schemes based on the Okubo-Weiss criterion, the vorticity magnitude, and Lagrangian coherent structures (LCSs), focusing on the inverse cascade in two-dimensional hydrodynamic turbulence. arxiv-2302-12971.title: BrainCLIP: Bridging Brain and Visual-Linguistic Representation Via CLIP for Generic Natural Visual Stimulus Decoding
arxiv-2302-12971.creator: Yulong Liu 1, Yongqiang Ma 1, Wei Zhou 1, Guibo Zhu 2, Nanning Zheng 1
arxiv-2302-12971.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yulong Liu 1, Yongqiang Ma 1, Wei Zhou 1, Guibo Zhu 2, Nanning Zheng 1. Due to the lack of paired samples and the low signal-to-noise ratio of functional MRI (fMRI) signals, reconstructing perceived natural images or decoding their semantic contents from fMRI data are challenging tasks. In this work, we propose, for the first time, a task-agnostic fMRI-based brain decoding model, BrainCLIP, which leverages CLIP’s cross-modal generalization ability to bridge the modality gap between brain activity, image, and text.

arxiv-2304-12362.title: Charged resonances and Minimal Dark Matter bound states at a multi-TeV muon collider
arxiv-2304-12362.creator: Natascia Vignaroli
arxiv-2304-12362.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Natascia Vignaroli. A multi-TeV muon collider proves to be very efficient not only for the search for new heavy neutral particles, but also for the discovery of charged bosons of the W ′ W^{\prime} type.

arxiv-2402-02098.title: Self-attention Networks Localize When QK-eigenspectrum Concentrates
arxiv-2402-02098.creator: Han Bao, Ryuichiro Hataya, Ryo Karakida
arxiv-2402-02098.description: Abstract The self-attention mechanism prevails in modern machine learning. It has an interesting functionality of adaptively selecting tokens from an input sequence by modulating the degree of attention localization, which many researchers speculate is the basis of the powerful model performance but complicates the underlying mechanism of the learning dynamics.

arxiv-2504-10289.title: Optimal Graph Stretching for Distributed Averaging
arxiv-2504-10289.creator: Florine W. Dekker, Zekeriya Erkin, Mauro Conti
arxiv-2504-10289.description: Abstract . The performance of distributed averaging depends heavily on the underlying topology. In various fields, including compressed sensing, multi-party computation, and abstract graph theory, graphs may be expected to be free of short cycles, i.e. to have high girth.

arxiv-2505-22450.title: Position: All Current Generative Fidelity and Diversity Metrics are Flawed
arxiv-2505-22450.creator: Ossi Räisä, Boris van Breugel, Mihaela van der Schaar
arxiv-2505-22450.description: Abstract Any method’s development and practical application is limited by our ability to measure its reliability. The popularity of generative modeling emphasizes the importance of good synthetic data metrics. Unfortunately, previous works have found many failure cases in current metrics, for example lack of outlier robustness and unclear lower and upper bounds.

pmc-12356869.title: Gene transcription, neurotransmitter, and neurocognition signatures of brain structural-functional coupling variability
pmc-12356869.creator: Lin Jiang, Sarah Genon, Jiayu Ye, Yan Zhu, Guangying Wang, Runyang He, Pedro A. Valdes-Sosa, Feng Wan, Dezhong Yao, Simon B. Eickhoff, Debo Dong, Fali Li, Peng Xu
pmc-12356869.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The relationship between brain structure and function, known as structural-functional coupling (SFC), is highly dynamic. However, the temporal variability of this relationship, referring to the fluctuating extent to which functional profiles interact with anatomy over time, remains poorly elucidated. Here, we propose a framework to quantify SFC temporal variability and determine its neurocognitive map, genetic architecture, and neurochemical basis in 1206 healthy human participants.

pmc-12466760.title: Correction: Omiya and Deguchi (2025). Adolescent Sense of Coherence over a Four-Year Period and the Pandemic: Junior and Senior High School Students Enrolled Before and After the Pandemic Broke out in Japan. Behavioral Sciences, 15(4), 504
pmc-12466760.creator: Tomoko Omiya, Naoko Kumada Deguchi
pmc-12466760.description: ntonovsky’s theory, we explored the importance of adolescent sense of coherence (SOC) in coping with stress and how it was affected by the pandemic. Using longitudinal data from junior and senior high school students in urban areas in Japan, we examined the trends in SOC and factors related to SOC in students enrolled before and after the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-12592885.title: Sociotechnical Challenges in Implementing Domestic Violence Screening via Telehealth and In-Person Care: Qualitative Study on Clinicians’ Perspectives
pmc-12592885.creator: Diana Freed, Marianne Sharko, Royoung Kim, Kelly Bartlett, Ermira Uldedaj, Natalie Bazarova, Lauri Goldkind
pmc-12592885.description: BackgroundNew York State Public Health Law Section 2805-z (NYSPHL§2805-z) mandates that hospitals implement certain protocols for the identification of domestic violence (DV) to strengthen support for DV survivors. However, there are challenges within our current health care delivery settings that raise critical questions about the effectiveness and adaptability of mandated policies for DV screening.

pmc-12912302.title: Reassessing the involvement of the CREB pathway in the circadian clock of Drosophila melanogaster
pmc-12912302.creator: Anna Katharina Eick, Maite Ogueta, Ralf Stanewsky
pmc-12912302.description: Circadian clocks are ubiquitous in almost all organisms on Earth and many key genes are highly conserved among species. In the mammalian suprachiasmatic nucleus, the cAMP response element binding protein (CREB) pathway is known to play a crucial role in conveying light-input to the transcription of clock genes.

pmc-13041515.title: Real-Time Polymerase Chain Reaction in Detecting Active Hepatitis C Virus Infection: A Retrospective Analysis
pmc-13041515.creator: Purvaja Muthukumarasamy, Priyadharshini Elumalai, Krithika Gopalakrishnan, Shanthi Mariappan, Sudhabharathi Reju
pmc-13041515.description: IntroductionHepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is a major worldwide health concern. It is a major cause of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and chronic hepatitis. Testing for anti-HCV antibodies is common for screening purposes, but it does not distinguish between an active and a past infection.

uslaw-usc-t40-s624.title: 40 U.S.C. § 624 — Information on certain leasing authorities
uslaw-usc-t40-s624.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t40-s624.description: United States Code, Title 40 (Public Buildings, Property, And Works); Chapter 5 (Property Management); Subchapter VII (Property Management). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— Except as provided in subsection (b), not later than December 31 of each year following the date of enactment of this subchapter, a Federal agency with independent leasing authority shall submit to the Council a list.
